translation_en: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to me, from Hisham, from Ma‘mar. And ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us; Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me, saying: Ibn ‘Abbas narrated to me, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to me, speaking directly to me. He said: During the period of truce between me and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, I set out. While I was in Syria, a letter from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was brought to Heraclius. Dihyah al-Kalbi had brought it and handed it to the governor of Busra, who then handed it to Heraclius. Heraclius said, ‘Is there anyone here from the people of this man who claims to be a prophet?’ They said, ‘Yes.’ I was summoned with a group of Quraysh, and we entered to see Heraclius. He seated us before him and said, ‘Which of you is closest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?’ Abu Sufyan said: I replied, ‘I am.’ They seated me before him and placed my companions behind me. Then he summoned his interpreter and said, ‘Tell them that I am going to question this man about the man who claims to be a prophet. If he lies to me, tell me that he is lying.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, had I not been afraid that they would report my lie, I would have lied. Then Heraclius said to his interpreter, ‘Ask him: What is his standing among you?’ I replied, ‘He is of noble standing among us.’ He asked, ‘Was any of his forefathers a king?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he has said?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Do the nobles follow him, or the weak?’ I replied, ‘Rather, the weak.’ He asked, ‘Are they increasing or decreasing?’ I replied, ‘They are increasing.’ He asked, ‘Does anyone among them abandon his religion out of resentment after entering it?’ I replied, ‘No.’ He asked, ‘Have you fought him?’ I replied, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘How has the fighting between you and him gone?’ I replied, ‘The war between us and him has gone back and forth: sometimes he has prevailed against us, and sometimes we have prevailed against him.’ He asked, ‘Does he betray?’ I replied, ‘No. During this period of truce with him, we do not know what he will do.’ Abu Sufyan said: By Allah, I could find no opportunity to add anything against him except that one remark. Heraclius asked, ‘Has anyone before him made this claim?’ I replied, ‘No.’ Then he said to his interpreter, ‘Tell him: I asked you about his standing among you, and you claimed that he is of noble standing among you. That is how messengers are sent from among the noble of their people. I asked whether any of his forefathers was a king, and you claimed that there was not. I said that if one of his forefathers had been a king, I would have thought that he was a man seeking his forefathers’ kingdom. I asked whether his followers were the weak or the nobles, and you said they were the weak; those are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether you had accused him of lying before he said what he has said, and you claimed that you had not. So I know that he would not leave lying to people and then go and lie about Allah. I asked whether anyone among them abandons his religion out of resentment after entering it, and you claimed that no one does. Such is faith when its delight enters the hearts. I asked whether they are increasing or decreasing, and you claimed they are increasing. Such is faith until it becomes complete. I asked whether you had fought him, and you claimed that you had, and that the war between you and him had gone back and forth: sometimes he prevailed against you and sometimes you prevailed against him. Such is the trial of messengers; then the outcome is theirs. I asked whether he betrays, and you claimed that he does not. Such is the way of messengers: they do not betray. I asked whether anyone before him had made this claim, and you claimed that no one had. I said that if anyone before him had made this claim, I would have thought that he was following a claim made before him.’ Then Heraclius said, ‘What does he command you to do?’ I replied, ‘He commands us to pray, give zakat, maintain ties of kinship, and remain chaste.’ He said, ‘If what you say about him is true, then he is a prophet. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think that he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would love to meet him. If I were with him, I would wash his feet. His dominion will surely reach what is beneath my feet.’ Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and read it. It said: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Submit, and you will be safe. Submit, and Allah will give you your reward twice over. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the ploughmen. “O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah…”’ through His words, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims’ (3:64). When he finished reading the letter, voices rose around him and the clamor grew loud. We were ordered out. Abu Sufyan said: When we came out, I said to my companions, ‘The matter of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become tremendous. The king of the Banu al-Asfar fears him.’ I remained certain that the matter of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would prevail until Allah brought Islam into my heart. Al-Zuhri said: Heraclius summoned the leading Romans and gathered them in a house of his. He said, ‘O Romans, would you like lasting success and right guidance, and for your kingdom to remain firmly established?’ They rushed toward the doors like wild donkeys, but found them locked. He said, ‘Bring them back to me.’ They were brought back, and he said, ‘I only tested how firmly you hold to your religion. I have now seen what I wanted to see from you.’ They prostrated to him and were pleased with him.
